description: Robustness set. Each case is a re-worded version of a gold case, deliberately constructed to share as few content words as possible with the gold phrasing. A system that only matches keywords will fail here. This set exists to evidence whether semantic matching is genuinely necessary, rather than asserting it.

cases.question: Freshly finished secondary school leaver here — which door do I walk through to sign up?
Trying to put my name down for a bachelors place.
I am a working professional, I want to deepen my qualification. Next step?
Someone told me my name is on the list. How do I see for myself?
I sent my forms weeks ago and heard nothing since.
The machine will not let me in anymore and I cannot remember what I typed.
The wifi keeps dropping every time I am in the lecture hall.
I need to see the marks for the courses I took last semester.
I want to add and drop subjects before the deadline.
Where are the lecture notes and materials hosted?
When does the semester start and when do examinations begin?
Is there a place online where I can look for vacancies after graduating?
I need to take a book back and extend it for longer.
What line do I call if I just want to speak to a human at reception?
Give me the exact spot on the map so I can tell a taxi driver.
I am a hiring manager and I want to set up something with your institution.
I am a developer and I need credentials to pull records from your farmers platform.
I am a producer and I want to make a movie. Do you teach that?
I want to join the free technology bootcamp you are advertising.
What will this cost me for the whole year?
cases.reason_special: Anti-hallucination test under lexical mismatch. A keyword matcher looking for 'fee' or 'tuition' will miss this entirely; a semantic matcher will not, and must still refuse to invent a figure.
